newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Stals repeats fx control must stay for now.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Stals repeats fx control must stay for now.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals reiterated in a newspaper interview on Wednesday that exchange controls must stay until foreign reserves improved.

He acknowledged that uncertainty about the timetable for lifting rand controls would lead to continued speculation in currency markets, but said the authorities had no choice than to hold their hand while reserves remained so low.
"As long as we have exchange controls, we will have the speculation," Stals told Business Rep ort.
"I agree that if we abolished exchange controls immediately it would solve the problem. But we can't do it until we have the foreign reserves.
"I think (those who call for quicker abolition of controls) are a little bit unreasonable."
Stals made the same point at an economic conference in Johannesburg last Friday, the day the rand started its latest fall to record lows on the foreign exchange markets.

He said then that when South African residents were given permission to invest rand savings offshore, there had to be some reasonable assurance that it would be possible for them to convert rand assets into foreign currencies with which they could acquire foreign investment.
"With its low level of foreign reserves, the Reserve Bank cannot provide this assurance. In our situation, to act precipitately could create disaster," Stals said on Friday.
South African reserves have declined from 15.7 billion rand at the end of 1995 to 10.0 billion rand at the end of September, equivalent to four weeks import cover.
